unresolvedMajorIssues: Horizontal gutters and the desktop shell position change from screen to screen, so the app does not read as one layout system
The workout screen shows fewer exercises per phone viewport than the baseline did

findings.evidence: On mobile the left gutter is about 16px on Today, Import error, Prompts and Library. It is about 28px on Routine detail and Workspace, about 42px on Import paste, about 44px on Routines and History, and about 56px on the Builder. Import paste and Import error are the same route but their content starts at different x positions. On desktop the sidebar sits at x≈28 on Prompts, x≈234 on Workout and x≈361 on Routines and History. Prompts content spans about 990px, while Routines and History are about 300px wide in the middle of an otherwise empty canvas. The sidebar also keeps a hamburger toggle inside the persistent nav.
findings.userConsequence: Moving between screens makes the page frame jump sideways and change width. Content sits against different edges on different pages, which looks unfinished. On desktop it is unclear what the layout is. Routines and History have large empty bands on both sides, while Prompts runs a preset field nearly 930px wide.
findings.suggestedChange: Use one mobile gutter, 16px or 20px, on every route. Use one desktop shell with a fixed sidebar position and a shared content max-width, with prose and form fields capped to a readable measure. Remove the redundant hamburger from the persistent desktop sidebar or give it a clear purpose.

findings.evidence: Each exercise card now spends a full row on the labeled tools History / Edit / Replace / Unit lb. The prescription, prescribed note, set row and note/rest row each sit on their own line. The first phone viewport shows the Warm-up card in full and only the top of Squat, whose set chips are cut off behind the sticky footer. The baseline phone capture showed three exercises. In the mobile captures the Squat rest timer and 'Start' control are not visible.
findings.userConsequence: The labels are clearer, but the logging screen takes more scrolling per exercise. During a set the user sees roughly one card instead of two or three. The sticky bar covers chips with no fade or edge, so they read as clipped.
findings.suggestedChange: Keep the text labels but put History as the main tool beside the exercise name. Move Edit, Replace and Unit into a labeled 'More' menu, or lay the tools out in a single compact row. Put the set chips and timer on one line. Add a top fade or padding above the sticky bar so rows scroll under it cleanly.

findings.evidence: Resolve shows '0 of 1 handled' with a disabled-looking 'Review import →'. Confirm then shows '4 exercises mapped to catalog' in green, 'Squat needs a specific version chosen.' under Review notes, and an unqualified dark 'Save program' button. The screens do not say whether saving with Squat unresolved is allowed or what happens to its history link. This matches an objection from the baseline Sol review (R00-SOL-06) and the implementation response does not address it.
findings.userConsequence: A user cannot tell whether the import is ready or is about to save an ambiguous mapping. The green success line and the unresolved note contradict each other.
findings.suggestedChange: Say which exercises are mapped and which are not, for example '3 mapped · 1 needs a version'. State what saving does with unresolved names, for example 'Squat will be saved without linked history'. Give the 'Review' button next to the note the main emphasis until resolved.

findings.evidence: The JSON textarea in Import paste and Import error is about 64px tall and shows two and a half lines of a long routine. The rest of the screen is blank. In Builder, 'Save routine' is the strongest control on a Day 1 with 'Strength 0 ex', and about 60% of the viewport is empty. The implementation response keeps this behavior on purpose because an empty day may be a rest day.
findings.userConsequence: The user cannot check what was pasted before validating. The builder gives no cue that a day with nothing in it will be saved as it is.
findings.suggestedChange: Make the textarea taller and grow it with its content, or show a line count under it. In the builder, label an empty section as 'Empty — will save as rest day', or warn before saving a routine in which every day is empty.

findings.evidence: The captures cut off at 'Appearance / Theme', so the theme control cannot be seen. The reported fix for the dark Workspace theme selection cannot be checked from the frozen image. The destructive 'Import workspace · Replace all local data — destructive' row is now outlined in orange, which is the same colour used for the storage and persistence warnings. The 'Storage usage' label wraps to two lines beside its value.
findings.userConsequence: This round's evidence does not show that the dark theme selection is fixed. The restore row looks like another warning, not like the one action that overwrites data.
findings.suggestedChange: Reorder or crop the Workspace capture so the Theme control is visible in both themes. Mark the restore row with a distinct danger treatment (red text or a separate 'Danger zone' group) and leave amber for advisory warnings.

findings.evidence: The desktop History capture shows 'Dumbbell Shoulder Press' with a darker highlight that reads as a selected row, though the surrounding rows do not. Desktop History still says 'Tap a movement to see every version and session.' The sort row reads 'sort · Sessions Name Recent', with the bullet marking the active option and no visible selected state. The filter chips 'all / recent / stale' have no explanation. Desktop Prompts keeps a 930px-wide preset name field and an unconstrained 'Name this preset…' row.
findings.userConsequence: A leftover hover or focus state looks like a selection. Mouse users are told to 'tap'. A new user cannot tell what 'stale' means or which sort is active.
findings.suggestedChange: Don't capture a hover state, or style hover and selection differently. Use 'Select a movement' on desktop. Show the active sort as a filled segmented control. Define 'stale' with a small hint, or rename it.

findings.evidence: Exercise history still shows 'VOL 2,025' with no unit (this matches baseline Sol finding R00-SOL-08). Version labels such as 'BARBELL SQUAT' are in very small monospace caps. The heatmap labels (M, W, F, S) and the profile card headings 'Body' and 'Training history' are about 11px or smaller, and the 'Body' card has extra empty space above its title. The green dot next to each day on Routine detail is not explained. Routine map cards (the 12 day tiles) have no chevron or other sign that they are tappable.
findings.userConsequence: Small, unlabeled details still make the numbers and status marks harder to read. The user may not know that the volume is in pounds, what the dot means, or that the map tiles open a day.
findings.suggestedChange: Add a unit to VOL, for example 'lb'. Raise the smallest labels to at least 12px. Add a short status label or a legend for the dot. Give map tiles a chevron or hover state.

findings.evidence: Every mobile screen repeats its title twice: the top-bar label on the right ('Today', 'Routines', 'Workout', 'Prompts') and the page heading below it. The top bar's right-hand label is light gray and small. Today step 1 is an outlined card with a dark button, while steps 2 and 3 use plain text links, so the three steps look unequal. Session summary hides the sticky bar behind the sheet, which is cleaner than baseline.
findings.userConsequence: The duplicate label uses space and adds noise without extra orientation. Steps 2 and 3 look like footnotes next to step 1, even though they are the next actions once step 1 is done.
findings.suggestedChange: Drop the right-hand top-bar label, or use it for contextual actions only. Give steps 2 and 3 the same button treatment (secondary) as the current-step button, and keep the primary treatment for whichever step is current.

strengths: The Prompts screen now puts one 'Copy prompt · 5,501 chars' primary button and a 'Go to Import' secondary button at the top, with coach text collapsed. This fixes the baseline objection from all three reviewers.
Today onboarding has numbered steps, a clear current-step action ('Go to Profile →') and a 'Build a routine manually' alternative.

Routine detail leads with 'Start workout', a one-line analysis summary with a 'View analysis' link, week tabs and a day list with 'View day' buttons. This is a clear improvement over the baseline analysis card.
Routines now has a page title, counts, 'New routine' and an 'Open' button on each row. Storage filenames and the 'OTHER' label are gone.
Page titles now follow one large-heading pattern on most screens, including Workspace, and the desktop sidebar adds persistent navigation.
Import errors show a bordered alert with 'Copy recovery prompt for your AI chat' as the main action. The file input is styled as a button.
History export puts Copy first, shows a populated preview with sessions/entries/sets counts, and does not imply an in-app AI.
Profile charts now have dates and starting and current values, and the heatmap has start and end dates.
Library chips wrap instead of being cut off, and the dark and light themes keep the same structure.
The session summary sheet is concise, hides the sticky bar behind it, and offers 'Review session' and 'Next day →'.
limitations: Review used only the 27 frozen static screenshots; I did not run or interact with the app, and I did not read any other current-round output.
Contrast is judged by eye. I measured no ratios, and the implementation response's token measurements are not independently verified here.
Dark theme is evidenced by four captures and desktop by four. Parity for the other screens, and responsive behavior outside 390×844 and 1280×900, is not shown.
Long pages (Profile, Prompts, Library, Workspace, Import confirm) were captured above the fold only, so the Theme control and content below are not reviewed.
Screenshots cannot show keyboard, screen-reader, touch-target, persistence or focus behavior. Pixel offsets and sizes above are visual estimates from the images.
Some baseline comparisons (workout density, desktop shell) were made against the baseline screenshots I opened; the other baseline screens were not re-opened except through the prior findings.
